title: Running Hot
subtitle: Mission 3 · 2 vs 2 · about 50 minutes
coachNotes: Two heavier ’Mechs join: the Catapult (missiles, can jump) and the Thunderbolt (tough brawler). Both have OV 1 on the card.
Overheat: before you roll, pick +1 damage in the shot. It only adds damage at short and medium range. You take the heat even if you miss.

Heat goes on the card at Clean up (the End Phase), so it hurts you next turn: +1 to your shots and 2 inches less walking per heat level. At heat 2 or more you are also 1 easier to hit, unless you jumped.
Heat 4 is the S box: the ’Mech shuts down. Next turn it can’t move or shoot, and shots at it get 4 easier. It restarts at heat 0 at that Clean up.
Cooling off: a turn where the ’Mech doesn’t shoot clears all its heat. Keep shooting and heat stays.
Overheat on the first turn is free-ish. Overheat every turn and you reach S at the end of turn 4, then sit out turn 5. Pick your moments.
The Locust and Commando can’t overheat. Use them to chase down a ’Mech that runs hot.
tableSteps: Use the same open table, about 3 feet across. Measure in inches and ignore printed hexes.
Put a hill in the middle and two patches of woods, one on each half. Hills, cover, and woods work like Broken Ground.
Keep a die or small token next to each ’Mech card to mark heat (0 to 3, then S). The app tracks it too.
Each side places its two ’Mechs within 6 inches of its own short table edge. After the first dice roll, the winner picks which side places first; then take turns placing one ’Mech at a time.
winningSummary: Knock out both enemy ’Mechs. If anyone is still standing after 8 turns, the side with more Structure left wins. Same Structure is a draw.

layout.openTable: No maps? Any open table about 36 × 22 inches works. Add the terrain where the diagram shows it.
